title: 2025 AMC 10B Problem 22
statement: A seven-digit positive integer is chosen at random. What is the probability that the number is divisible by \(11,\) given that the sum of its digits is \(61?\)

solutions.text: A digit sum of \(61 = 63 - 2\) means all seven digits are \(9\) except for a total deficit of \(2,\) which gives \(\binom{2 + 6}{6} = 28\) numbers. For divisibility by \(11\) we need \(O - E \equiv 0 \pmod{11},\) where \(O\) sums the \(4\) odd-position digits and \(E\) the \(3\) even ones. Write the deficits as \(d_O + d_E = 2.\) Then \(O - E = 9 - d_O\) \(+ d_E = 11 - 2 d_O,\) a multiple of \(11\) only when \(d_O = 0.\) So all of the deficit \(2\) falls on the \(3\) even positions, giving \(\binom{2 + 2}{2} = 6\) ways. The probability is \(\tfrac{6}{28} = \tfrac{3}{14}.\) Therefore, the answer is A.
hints: A digit sum of \(61\) is \(2\) below the maximum \(63,\) so the digits are all \(9\) except a total shortfall of \(2\)
For divisibility by \(11\) use the alternating digit sum; express it through the shortfalls on the odd- versus even-position digits
